ARCHITECTURE.md describes five stages, but the RTL has a sixth register stage (the y/acc output register) before done.'
- about: go_priority
  text: 'A GO write always wins over a simultaneous done in dotq_regs.sv (READY ends 0). A new go while a computation is in flight also cancels it in dotq_core.sv: every valid stage is gated with ~go, so the earlier result is dropped, and the new computation restarts from the loaded operands. Operand writes during a computation are not blocked and can corrupt that result; the spec calls this out of contract.'
- about: result_visibility
  text: 'Y and ACC are not cleared by GO; the core keeps the old values and dotq_regs.sv only masks them to 0 on reads while READY is 0. The y/acc registers in the core are overwritten when a computation completes, slightly before READY rises.'
- about: unmapped_access
  text: 'Reads of 0x07 (GO) and of 0x0B-0x7F return 0; writes to RO registers (0x08-0x0A) and to 0x0B-0x7F are ignored with no error response (dotq_regs.sv default branches). A write to any address other than 0x07 never starts a computation. Writes to MULT keep only bits [15:0]; writes to CTRL keep only bits [4:0] and [8].'
- about: window_address
  text: 'The register offsets in this document are window-relative. The shell reaches the design only for shell addresses with bit 7 set, so A_LO is at shell address 0x80 and STATUS at 0x8A (shell_core.sv: win_addr is addr[6:0]). Shell addresses 0x00-0x05 are the shell''s own registers (design ID, version, build stamp, scratch, error counters, build ID). A window read returns its data after a registered read, one cycle after win_rd.'
- about: ctrl_shift_range
  text: 'CTRL accepts any 5-bit shift. The RTL handles shift 0 (no rounding constant is added, so the result is the plain product) although the spec only defines 1..31. Reset value of shift is 1, of relu 0.'
- about: clamp_order
  text: 'dotq_core.sv checks the upper clamp (127) first, then relu (below 0 gives 0), then the lower clamp (-128 gives 0x80). Y is returned as 8 bits, zero-extended in the register read; a negative y therefore reads as 0x80..0xFF in bits [7:0] with bits [31:8] zero, not sign-extended.'
- about: port_name_spec
  text: 'spec.yaml names the LED port LED0; the built top-level port is the bus LED[0] (rtl/c14_int8_dot_requant_top.sv, design.xdc, pin H17). The RTL and XDC are what was built. LED0 exists only as an internal net, which is what the checker binds to.'
- about: reset_timing
  text: 'The spec says outputs and READY clear within 2 cycles of CPU_RESETN asserting. In the RTL (shell/rtl/reset_sync.sv) assertion of rst is asynchronous, but the design flops clear on the next clock edge while rst is high; release needs two clock edges after the button is let go. The 2-cycle figure was not measured.'
- about: design_id_parameter
  text: 'The spec lists DESIGN_ID among the parameters; in the RTL it is a localparam in the top file and cannot be set from outside. It reaches the shell at address 0x00.'
- about: assumptions
  text: 'Assumptions made by the run (spec.yaml): the clock is 100 MHz so CLKS_PER_BIT is 868; weights are never -128 (the design still computes correctly with them); acc never overflows 32 bits for the tested inputs; operand writes during a computation are not required to be safe; shift outside 1..31 is out of contract. summary: 'The design computes an 8-way signed int8 dot product plus a 32-bit bias, multiplies the sum by a 16-bit unsigned
  multiplier, applies a rounding right shift (halves round towards plus infinity) and clamps the result to a signed 8-bit
  value, with an optional ReLU. It sits behind the reusable UART test shell on the Nexys A7-100T (xc7a100tcsg324-1) and
  is driven by register reads and writes over the USB-UART. The run reached simulation level V2 of V3: verification stopped
  at V3 because five cover properties were never hit, so no synthesis, implementation or hardware result exists. The specification
  and architecture were accepted automatically by a model, with no human review.'
scope_not:
- 'Not a general neural-network layer: one 8-element dot product per GO, with no streaming, batching or accumulation across
  calls.'
- 'Not a design with a defined overflow or wrap behaviour: acc overflow and shift outside 1..31 are out of contract and
  untested.'
- Not hardware-verified, not timing-closed and not measured for resources or power; none of those stages ran.
target:
  part: xc7a100tcsg324-1
  board: nexys_a7_100t
  tool: Vivado 2026.1
  top: c14_int8_dot_requant_top
clocks:
- name: CLK100MHZ
  mhz: 100.0
  source: results/68_agent_docs/20261107-005621-8deb/c14_int8_dot_requant/design.xdc
resets:
- name: CPU_RESETN
  active: low
  note: 'Board button on pin C12. rtl/c14_int8_dot_requant_top.sv passes it through shell/rtl/reset_sync.sv: assertion is
    asynchronous, release is synchronous after two clock edges, and the resulting active-high reset is applied synchronously
    in all blocks. It clears the operand registers, y, acc and READY, and sets CTRL to shift 1, relu 0.'
interfaces:
- name: CLK100MHZ
  type: clock input
  note: Board 100 MHz oscillator on pin E3, LVCMOS33; the single clock for shell and arithmetic, constrained at a 10.00
    ns period in design.xdc.
- name: UART_TXD_IN
  type: UART serial input (8N1, 115200 baud)
  note: 'Pin C4: data from the host into the FPGA. Asynchronous; it is synchronised in the shell by sync2. design.xdc gives
    it a 2.0 max / 0.0 min input delay.'
- name: UART_RXD_OUT
  type: UART serial output (8N1, 115200 baud)
  note: 'Pin D4: data from the FPGA to the host. The shell protocol is shell/PROTOCOL.md. design.xdc gives it a 2.0 max
    / 0.0 min output delay.'
- name: LED0
  type: LED output
  note: Shows the READY flag. The built top-level port is the bus LED[0] on pin H17 (rtl/c14_int8_dot_requant_top.sv, design.xdc);
    the spec calls it LED0, which is only an internal net in the RTL.
registers:
- offset: '0x00'

  access: RW
  reset: '0x00000000'
  bits: '[31:0] activations 0..3, a_i in bits [8i+7:8i]'
- offset: '0x01'
  name: A_HI
  access: RW
  reset: '0x00000000'
  bits: '[31:0] activations 4..7, a_(4+i) in bits [8i+7:8i]'
- offset: '0x02'
  name: W_LO
  access: RW
  reset: '0x00000000'
  bits: '[31:0] weights 0..3, same packing'
- offset: '0x03'
  name: W_HI
  access: RW
  reset: '0x00000000'
  bits: '[31:0] weights 4..7, same packing'
- offset: '0x04'
  name: BIAS
  access: RW
  reset: '0x00000000'
  bits: '[31:0] signed bias'
- offset: '0x05'
  name: MULT
  access: RW
  reset: '0x00000000'
  bits: '[15:0] unsigned multiplier; [31:16] read 0'
- offset: '0x06'
  name: CTRL
  access: RW
  reset: '0x00000001'
  bits: '[4:0] shift (1..31), [8] relu; other bits read 0'
- offset: '0x07'
  name: GO
  access: WO
  reset: '0x00000000'
  bits: any write starts one computation; reads 0
- offset: '0x08'
  name: Y
  access: RO
  reset: '0x00000000'
  bits: '[7:0] limited answer (two''s complement); [31:8] read 0'
- offset: '0x09'
  name: ACC
  access: RO
  reset: '0x00000000'
  bits: '[31:0] the signed accumulator including the bias'
- offset: '0x0A'
  name: STATUS
  access: RO
  reset: '0x00000000'
  bits: '[0] READY; other bits 0'
parameters:
- name: CLKS_PER_BIT
  value: 868
  legal: Positive integer; only 868 (100 MHz / 115200 baud) was designed for and tested.
  note: UART clocks per bit, giving 115200 baud 8N1 on CLK100MHZ. Any other value changes the baud rate.
- name: TIMEOUT_CYCLES
  value: 100000000
  legal: Positive integer.
  note: Clocks of silence after which the shell drops a partly received frame without a response. The top overrides the
    shell's own smaller default.
- name: BUILD_STAMP
  value: 0
  legal: Any 32-bit value.
  note: Read back through the shell at its address 0x02; the spec says the flow overrides the default of 0. It does not
    affect the arithmetic.
- name: DESIGN_ID
  value: DOTQ
  legal: 'Fixed: 0x444F5451 (ASCII D,O,T,Q).'
  note: This is a localparam in rtl/c14_int8_dot_requant_top.sv, not an overridable top-level parameter. The shell returns
    it at its address 0x00.

- about: latency_count
  text: 'Counted from rtl/dotq_core.sv and rtl/dotq_regs.sv: with the one-cycle go pulse in cycle 0, v1..v5 follow, done
    is high in cycle 6 and READY is high in cycle 7, so READY rises 7 clocks after the go pulse, or 8 clocks after the shell
    write strobe because dotq_regs registers go. This meets the spec''s "within 8 clocks" only if the count starts at the
    go pulse or the write strobe exactly; it has no margin. ARCHITECTURE.md describes five stages, but the RTL has a sixth
    register stage (the y/acc output register) before done.'
- about: go_priority
  text: 'A GO write always wins over a simultaneous done in dotq_regs.sv (READY ends 0). A new go while a computation is
    in flight also cancels it in dotq_core.sv: every valid stage is gated with ~go, so the earlier result is dropped, and
    the new computation restarts from the loaded operands. Operand writes during a computation are not blocked and can corrupt
    that result; the spec calls this out of contract.'
- about: result_visibility
  text: Y and ACC are not cleared by GO; the core keeps the old values and dotq_regs.sv only masks them to 0 on reads while
    READY is 0. The y/acc registers in the core are overwritten when a computation completes, slightly before READY rises.
- about: unmapped_access
  text: Reads of GO and of every offset above STATUS return 0; writes to the RO registers (Y, ACC, STATUS) and to every
    offset above STATUS are ignored with no error response (dotq_regs.sv default branches). A write to any address other
    than GO never starts a computation. Writes to MULT keep only bits [15:0]; writes to CTRL keep only bits [4:0] and [8].
- about: window_address
  text: 'The register offsets in this document are window-relative. The shell reaches the design only for shell addresses
    with bit 7 set, and the window offset is the low 7 bits (shell_core.sv: win_addr is addr[6:0]), so A_LO is at shell
    address 0x80 and each later register follows at the next address. Shell addresses with bit 7 clear are the shell''s
    own registers (design ID, version, build stamp, scratch, error counters, build ID). A window read returns its data after
    a registered read, one cycle after win_rd.'
- about: ctrl_shift_range
  text: CTRL accepts any 5-bit shift. The RTL handles shift 0 (no rounding constant is added, so the result is the plain
    product) although the spec only defines 1..31. Reset value of shift is 1, of relu 0.
- about: clamp_order
  text: dotq_core.sv checks the upper clamp (127) first, then relu (below 0 gives 0), then the lower clamp (-128 gives the
    byte 0x80). Y is returned as 8 bits, zero-extended in the register read; a negative y therefore reads as its two's-complement
    byte in bits [7:0] with bits [31:8] zero, not sign-extended.
- about: port_name_spec
  text: spec.yaml names the LED port LED0; the built top-level port is the bus LED[0] (rtl/c14_int8_dot_requant_top.sv,
    design.xdc, pin H17). The RTL and XDC are what was built. LED0 exists only as an internal net, which is what the checker
    binds to.
- about: reset_timing
  text: The spec says outputs and READY clear within 2 cycles of CPU_RESETN asserting. In the RTL (shell/rtl/reset_sync.sv)
    assertion of rst is asynchronous, but the design flops clear on the next clock edge while rst is high; release needs
    two clock edges after the button is let go. The 2-cycle figure was not measured.
- about: design_id_parameter
  text: The spec lists DESIGN_ID among the parameters; in the RTL it is a localparam in the top file and cannot be set from
    outside. It reaches the shell at address 0x00.
- about: assumptions
  text: 'Assumptions made by the run (spec.yaml): the clock is 100 MHz so CLKS_PER_BIT is 868; weights are never -128 (the
    design still computes correctly with them); acc never overflows 32 bits for the tested inputs; operand writes during
    a computation are not required to be safe; shift outside 1..31 is out of contract. TIMEOUT_CYCLES and BUILD_STAMP defaults
    and the DOTQ ID presentation were defaulted by the oracle, not answered.'
